title: Welcome to Korea
culture: Greet airport staff politely. A small bow is common; use everyday polite speech with people you do not know.
objectives: Greet someone and choose a farewell for who is leaving.
Introduce your name and identify yourself politely.
Thank someone, apologize, and make a simple request.
Confirm understanding and ask for repetition.

title: Read Your First Korean Words
culture: Hangul letters combine into syllable blocks. Romanization is a temporary aid, not a pronunciation system that replaces listening.
objectives: Recognize consonants, vowels, and syllable blocks.
Distinguish basic consonants and vowel orientations.
Assemble blocks and read short words.
Decode useful signs without relying on romanization.

title: Making New Friends
culture: Use polite speech with new acquaintances, even when they seem your age. Ask before switching to casual speech.
objectives: Ask about origin and distinguish nationality from language.
Ask about occupations without assuming someone’s role.
Identify nearby objects and ask what they are.
Say what you like using an object particle.

title: Shopping in Korea
culture: Korean uses two number systems. Prices use Sino-Korean numbers; many counters use native numbers with shortened forms.
objectives: Count one to eight and recognize counter forms.
Read prices and combine units of ten, hundred, and thousand.
Ask a price and choose a payment method.
Ask for an item and a different size politely.

title: Taste of Korea
culture: Food names do not reliably identify every ingredient. Ask staff about ingredients and allergies; do not assume a dish is vegetarian or allergen-free.
objectives: Recognize common dishes and ask about ingredients.
Place an order and ask about ingredients.
Order drinks using appropriate counters.
Describe taste and ask for a less spicy option.

title: Getting Around Korea
culture: Follow station signage and priority seating rules. Check the line and direction; a station name alone does not identify the correct platform.
objectives: Name useful places and state a destination.
Understand a short direction sequence.
Ask for a station and recognize boarding vocabulary.
Ask and explain where something is located.

title: Everyday Life in Korea
culture: Bukchon includes residential streets. Keep voices low, follow visiting-hour signs, and ask before photographing residents.
objectives: Recognize weekdays and ask the date.
Tell hours and minutes with the correct number system.
Describe a routine using polite present tense.
Describe a completed past action.

title: Korean Culture and Manners
culture: Courtesy depends on relationship and situation, not age alone. Use respectful titles and follow photography and access rules at heritage sites.
objectives: Distinguish polite conversation from casual forms.
Use respectful titles and familiar respectful requests.
Ask permission and recognize restrictions.
Name major holidays and discuss a cultural activity.

title: My Korean Travel Diary
culture: Busan has regional speech, but standard polite Korean is widely understood. Stay on marked coastal paths and follow weather warnings.
objectives: Describe weather and distinguish seasonal vocabulary.
Describe scenery and compare an impression.
State an intended future plan with a time and destination.
Write a short account of a trip and a future plan.

title: Korean Adventure Finale
culture: Use what you know to solve everyday travel tasks. Ask for clarification rather than pretending to understand.
objectives: Greet, introduce yourself, and ask a follow-up question.
Order, pay, and ask for directions in sequence.
Read signs and compose short sentences in Hangul.
Combine requests, permission, past experience, and a plan.
